page: Google Cloud Platform n2-highcpu-8 is an x86_64 architecture server instance belonging to the n2 family. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.8 GHz, configured as 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The instance is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low memory-to-core ratio of 1.0 GB per vCPU. It does not include local storage or integrated GPU hardware. The processor features a 33 MB L3 cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 KB L1d cache, alongside hardware support for AVX-512 vector extensions, AES cryptography, and Intel Hyper-Threading.

Benchmark data indicates average multi-core performance, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 7430.34 and a PassMark CPU score of 8305.34. However, single-core performance is weak, as shown by a stress-ng single-core score of 1409.67 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1138.0. Memory performance is constrained, with a weak PassMark memory score of 1328.72, though cached read-only memory bandwidth reaches an average of 412.9 GB/sec. The instance demonstrates average capabilities in software compilation, text processing, and static web serving, but struggles with memory-intensive tasks, image processing, and ray tracing.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the n2-highcpu-8 offers a high density of dedicated compute cores relative to its memory footprint. This makes it a resource-efficient option for CPU-bound workloads that do not require large memory allocations. It is suitable for tasks such as software compilation, static web serving, text processing, and basic multi-threaded batch processing. It is not recommended for memory-intensive databases, large-scale data science, or workloads requiring local NVMe storage or GPU acceleration.
description: Google Cloud Platform n2-highcpu-8 is an x86_64 compute-optimized server instance featuring 8 dedicated vCPUs and 8.0 GB of RAM, powered by an Intel Xeon processor at 2.8 GHz. It contains 4 physical cores with hyper-threading, a 33 MB L3 cache, and lacks local storage or GPU accelerators. Performance benchmarks show average multi-core capabilities, including a stress-ng multi-core score of 7430.34 and a static web serving throughput of 6.62 GB/sec. However, single-core performance and memory scores are weak, reflecting the instance's low memory-to-core ratio of 1.0 GB per vCPU. This configuration provides a cost-effective option for CPU-bound tasks with low memory requirements, such as software compilation, text processing, and static web serving, while remaining unsuitable for memory-heavy databases or data-intensive applications.
